sections.h2: Finding the Mitchell County recording counter
sections.html:
The office is Suite 4 at 26 Crimson Laurel Circle, Bakersville, NC 28705. It is open on weekdays except holidays and records from 8:00 until 4:30. Call 828.688.2139. Extension 1401 handles fee and recording questions, and extension 1402 reaches the register's line. The fax number is 828-688-3666.

Marriage licenses are written until 4:00 and cost $60, payable by check, cash or money order. Recording itself can be paid in cash, by card, check or money order.

Staff act only as a recording office, and state law bars the register and employees from practicing law. Any question about what a deed should say goes to an attorney.

At mitchelldeeds.com you will find real estate indexes and images from 1994 to the present. Older material, from 1861 through 1993, sits in the Index Book Viewer under the search menu. The county's services list also covers vital records, an online vital request, document recording standards, index standards and a page for redacting personal information.

The 1994 line matters if your family has held land for generations. A deed of trust from the early nineties, a right-of-way, or a division of a family tract may appear only in the older books.

  • Search the current index under your name and the prior owner's name.
  • Open the Index Book Viewer when the chain of title reaches back before 1994.
  • Write down every deed of trust you find and confirm each has a recorded satisfaction.

Your closing attorney still performs the formal title search. A pass of your own simply tells you whether surprises are likely.

Mitchell County is small and settled: 15,062 residents and 8,785 housing units as of July 1, 2025, with 6,587 households in the survey ending 2024. Median rent is $813, owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,275 a month in costs, and 90.1 percent of residents lived in the same home a year earlier. Builders pulled 44 permits in 2025.

For an inherited house, gather the death certificate, the prior deed and any recorded deeds of trust before you meet with a closing attorney.

The posted fee schedule cites G.S. 161-10 and took effect October 1, 2016. Amounts:

Mitchell County recording fees
Document or servicePosted amount
Deed of trust$64.00 for 35 pages, $4.00 each page after
Other instruments, such as a deed$26.00 for 15 pages, $4.00 each page after
Plat$21.00 a page, 18 by 24 inch sheets only
UCC filing$38.00 for 1 to 2 pages, $45.00 for 3 to 10
SatisfactionNo fee
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each additional

A UCC filing over ten pages is $45.00 plus $2.00 for every page past ten. If a figure matters for your closing, call 828-688-2139 extension 1401 before you send a check.

Yes, the office accepts e-recording through Simplifile or CSC, the two vendors on its e-recording page.

Law firms and title companies commonly submit this way, so ask your closing attorney which route the firm uses. A paper document you file yourself, such as a corrective deed or a gift deed, can go to Suite 4 on any weekday.

The seller pays it in Bakersville when the deed is submitted. G.S. 105-228.30 sets the rate at one dollar per $500 of price, rounding a partial $500 up.

The county holds half and sends the state half, less refunds and a 2 percent county allowance on the state portion.

The tax depends on your actual deed price, so read the number off your settlement statement rather than estimating.

The office keeps birth, death and marriage records, current and historical, and offers an online vital request. Anyone can obtain a copy of a vital record, but state law restricts who may receive certified copies, so check the vital records page for the list.

A marriage license is $60 and is issued on weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00. Call ahead for the requirements before you drive over.

G.S. 47-18 says unrecorded transfers and options give way to lien creditors and paying purchasers, and that rank follows the time of registration. Registration happens in the county where the land sits, so Mitchell parcels are registered in Bakersville.

Ask when the buyer's deed is expected to appear in the index. County voters choose the register every two years under G.S. 161-1.

Most of the work happens before anyone visits Suite 4.

  • Pull your current deed and confirm that the names and legal description are right.
  • List each loan against the house and ask each lender when it will file its satisfaction. Filing is free, but the lender has to send it.
  • Decide whether your attorney will submit electronically or whether you will bring paper to Bakersville.
  • Confirm the total with the office at extension 1401 if the document runs long, since extra pages add $4.00 each.

Once the deed is recorded, keep the stamped copy or the confirmation from the e-recording vendor. It is your proof of filing, and the next owner's title search will begin with it.

Sign up for the office's free Fraud Alert system, which warns you if someone tries to change records tied to your property. It helps most with vacant, rental and inherited houses.

  • Keep copies of every deed, release and satisfaction you receive.
  • Search your name in the index every so often.
  • Record inherited or gifted property promptly.

Anyone buying on an installment land contract should read Chapter 47H, which requires the seller to put the contract, or a short memorandum of it, on record within five business days.

sections.h2: Other county offices in a house sale
sections.html:
Three offices touch the same sale. The register records the deed. The Tax Collector at 61 Crimson Laurel Circle takes payment of the year's bill. The Tax Assessor at Suite 5, next door to the register, handles relief applications. Bills go to the January 1 owner of record in August, so the closing papers need to say who covers the year.

Property tax relief for a disabled veteran or an older owner is applied for through the assessor on Form AV-9, with Form NCDVA-9 added for the disabled veteran exclusion after a visit with a veteran service officer. Neither claim is filed with the Register of Deeds. The register's office handles related paper, such as recorded deeds and discharge records, but the relief decision is the assessor's. Ask that office which documents it wants before the next January listing period.

A cash buyer of an inherited Mitchell County house can close as-is, with the deed filed through a closing attorney at settlement.

faqs.q: Which phone line reaches Mitchell County recording staff?
faqs.a: Call 828-688-2139 and use extension 1401 for fees and recording, or extension 1402 for the register's line. The office is at 26 Crimson Laurel Circle, Suite 4, Bakersville.

faqs.q: How old are the Mitchell County records I can search online?
faqs.a: The online index holds real estate indexes and images from 1994 to the present. The 1861 through 1993 material is in the Index Book Viewer on the search menu.

faqs.q: Does filing a mortgage satisfaction cost money in Mitchell County?
Can my attorney e-record a Mitchell County deed?
faqs.a: Yes, through Simplifile and CSC, the two vendors the office uses for e-recording.

faqs.q: Will the recording staff tell me what my deed should say?
faqs.a: No. The office acts as a recording office only, and state law keeps the register and staff from practicing law. Ask an attorney about wording, title or rights.
